abstract: >
  **Background:** Identification of modifiable causal drivers of opioid
  use disorder (OUD)-related emergency department (ED) visits before onset
  of dependence is a clinical priority.
  Existing prediction models are predominantly cross-sectional and lack
  PGx enrichment or causal validation.
  **Methods:** We constructed a retrospective cohort from a state-level
  All-Payer Claims Database (APCD; 2016–2019), targeting adults aged 13–64
  years with opioid-related ED visits (ICD-10: F11.xx; $n$ = 26,710 cases,
  180,640 matched controls).
  A three-model ensemble (CatBoost, XGBoost, XGBoost-RF) was trained on
  2016–2018 data and evaluated on a prospective 2019 holdout.
  Causal features were identified using the Consensus Filter (SHAP ∩ Formal
  Feature Attribution), and patient trajectories were characterized via
  Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) clustering and BupaR pre-diagnosis process maps.
  **Results:** The ensemble achieved mean PR-AUC = 0.88 ± 0.03 and
  AUROC = 0.96 ± 0.01 on the 2019 holdout across four age bands.
  Consensus-Causal features included gabapentin, long-term opioid use
  (ICD-10: Z79891), and the PGx polydrug exposure score
  (SHAP rank ≥ 90th percentile; FFA support ≥ 0.10).
  DTW clustering identified two dominant trajectory archetypes: Rapid-Onset
  (acute injury → high-dose escalation, median 4.2 months to OUD diagnosis)
  and Chronic-Escalation (long-term pain → dose creep, median 22.1 months).
  **Conclusions:** Ensemble modeling with Consensus Filter feature selection
  identifies robust, modifiable causal drivers of OUD-related ED visits up
  to two years before diagnosis, enabling proactive, trajectory-informed
  clinical intervention.

# Background {#sec-background}

Opioid use disorder (OUD) affects approximately 2.7 million Americans and
contributes to more than 80,000 opioid-related deaths and 1.5 million ED
visits annually [@Mattson2021; @Vivolo2018].
The active workforce and young adult population (ages 13–64) bear a
disproportionate burden, with opioid-related ED utilization concentrated in
this age range [@Hudgins2019].

Identifying high-risk trajectories before dependence diagnosis (ICD-10: F11.20)
enables cost-effective intervention [@Dowell2022].
Most published risk models are static at the time of clinical encounter and
ignore the longitudinal prescription and diagnosis sequences available in
administrative claims data.

Pharmacogenomic (PGx) factors further complicate individual opioid risk:
CYP2D6 poor metabolizers accumulate higher active metabolite concentrations
from hydrocodone and oxycodone, while CYP2D6 ultrarapid metabolizers derive
inadequate analgesia from codeine and may escalate doses [@Crews2021].
Despite these established mechanisms, PGx features are absent from nearly
all published OUD prediction models (Chapter 1).

This study applies the partition-first, Consensus Filter methodology
(Chapter 2) to the opioid ED cohort to:

1. Develop and validate an ensemble model predicting opioid-related ED visits
   across four age bands (13–24, 25–44, 45–54, 55–64 years).
2. Identify Consensus-Causal features—confirmed by both SHAP and FFA—as
   modifiable intervention targets.
3. Characterize pre-diagnosis patient trajectories using DTW clustering to
   define clinically distinct risk archetypes.

# Methods {#sec-methods}

## Study Design and Data Source

This retrospective cohort study used Virginia's All-Payer Claims Database
(APCD; 2016–2019) under a data use agreement with the Virginia Center for
Health Innovation (VCHI) and the Virginia Health Information (VHI).
The study was classified as non-human-subjects research
(IRB waiver: HM20022300).
Reporting follows TRIPOD guidelines for prediction model studies.

## Cohort Construction {#sec-cohort}

**Case definition:** Patients with ≥1 opioid use disorder diagnosis
(ICD-10: F11.xx) appearing in any of 10 diagnosis columns of an ED claim
(Milliman HCG code: O11 or P51) during 2016–2019.
Cases required ≥12 months of continuous enrollment prior to the index ED
visit to ensure adequate exposure history.

**Exclusion criteria:** Age < 13 or > 64 years; < 12 months enrollment;
any prior OUD diagnosis (washout period—prevalent cases excluded to
target *incident* OUD).

**Control definition:** Patients with zero opioid-related ICD codes
(F11.xx, T40.xx), matched to cases 5:1 without replacement by
age band (within 2 years), sex, and enrollment duration.

**Temporal safeguard:** All features were derived exclusively from the period
*prior* to the index ED date (cases) or matched index date (controls).
Events on or after the index date were excluded to prevent target leakage.

Age bands: 13–24, 25–44, 45–54, 55–64 years, aligned to developmental and
prescribing-pattern archetypes.

## Feature Engineering

**Input feature domains:**

- *Drug exposure*: NDC → generic drug name mapping; count and binary
  presence of 487 drug classes in the pre-index window
- *Diagnosis codes*: ICD-10 category counts (all 10 diagnosis columns)
- *Procedure codes*: CPT-4 category counts
- *PGx interaction scores*: CPIC Level A/B gene-drug interaction counts
  for CYP2D6, CYP2C9, CYP2C19, OPRM1 [@Crews2021]
- *Temporal density metrics*: claim count per month, inter-claim intervals

**MCCV feature screening:** 50 random train-test splits on 2016–2018 training
data; features retained if median recall-weighted rank ≥ 25th percentile.

**Process mining (visualization only):** BupaR pre-F11.20 event sequences
and FP-Growth drug co-occurrence networks were computed for *training cohort
only* and used exclusively for trajectory visualization; these outputs were
**not** included as predictive features.

## Ensemble Model and Consensus Filter

The three-model ensemble (CatBoost, XGBoost, XGBoost-RF) and Consensus Filter
are described in detail in Chapter 2.
In brief: model weights were derived from MCCV PR-AUC and LogLoss metrics;
Consensus-Causal features required SHAP rank ≥ 75th percentile **and** FFA
support ≥ 0.05 with confidence ≥ 0.70.

## Trajectory Analysis {#sec-trajectory}

**DTW clustering:** Dynamic Time Warping [@Berndt1994] distance matrices were
computed on event-type sequences (drug, diagnosis, procedure codes) for the
12-month pre-index window.
Hierarchical clustering (Ward linkage) was applied to the DTW distance matrix.
The optimal number of clusters was selected by minimizing within-cluster sum
of squared DTW distances, evaluated at $k$ = 2–8.

**BupaR pre-diagnosis maps:** Process maps were rendered from the training
cohort showing the most frequent event transitions preceding the first F11.20
diagnosis, filtered to events occurring > 30 days before diagnosis.

## Statistical Analysis

Model performance was evaluated on the 2019 temporal holdout using AUROC,
PR-AUC, Brier score, and LogLoss.
Class imbalance (5:1 case-control ratio) was addressed with scale-pos-weight
adjustment in XGBoost and class-weight balancing in CatBoost.
Calibration was assessed via reliability diagrams (10-bin) and the
integrated calibration index (ICI).
All analyses used Python 3.11 (scikit-learn 1.3, SHAP 0.44,
CatBoost 1.2, XGBoost 2.0).

## Predictive Performance {#sec-performance}

Ensemble performance on the 2019 temporal holdout is summarized by age band
in **@tbl-performance** and **@fig-curves**.
The 25–44 year band achieved the highest PR-AUC (0.889 ± 0.03), consistent
with the high opioid prescription burden in this working-age stratum.
The 13–24 band showed the lowest PR-AUC (0.835 ± 0.04), reflecting smaller
case counts and fewer prescription signals in younger patients.

## Consensus-Causal Features {#sec-causal-features}

Across all four age bands, 384–498 features met the Consensus-Causal threshold
(SHAP ≥ 75th pct AND FFA support ≥ 0.05; 384 for the 13–24 band, 498 for 25–64).
Top features by mean |SHAP| across bands are shown in **@fig-shap**.

The highest-ranked Consensus-Causal features were:

1. **Gabapentin** count (opioid adjunct; mean |SHAP| = 0.34, 25–44 band)
2. **Long-term opioid use (Z79891)** (chronic exposure marker; top ICD 45–64 bands)
3. **PGx polydrug exposure score** (pgx_num_drugs; mean |SHAP| = 2.22, rank #1)
4. **[Drug B] AND NOT [Drug C]** (FFA rule; support = [0.XX], conf = [0.XX])
5. **Claim density** in 90-day pre-index window (mean |SHAP| = 1.49, n_events)

A representative FFA rule for the 25–44 age band:

```
IF (Oxycodone_count ≥ 2) AND (ChronicPainDx = TRUE)
   AND NOT (PhysicalTherapy_count ≥ 1)
THEN P(OUD-ED) ↑↑   [support = 0.12, confidence = 0.83]
```

Features selected by both SHAP and FFA are marked with ★.](../figures/ch03/fig_shap.pdf){#fig-shap

## Trajectory Analysis {#sec-trajectories}

DTW clustering on the 12-month pre-diagnosis event sequence identified
$k$ = 2 as the optimal cluster count (elbow criterion), yielding two
clinically distinct archetypes (**@fig-trajectories**):

**Cluster 1 – Rapid-Onset** ($n$ = [XX,XXX]; [XX%] of cases):
Mean time from first opioid prescription to OUD-ED: 4.2 months (SD 1.8).
Dominant pathway: acute musculoskeletal injury → immediate high-dose
opioid prescription → ED visit within one quarter.
BupaR process map showed minimal intervening non-opioid pain management.

**Cluster 2 – Chronic-Escalation** ($n$ = [XX,XXX]; [XX%] of cases):
Mean time from first opioid prescription to OUD-ED: 22.1 months (SD 8.4).
Dominant pathway: chronic pain diagnosis → incremental dose escalation
→ addition of benzodiazepine → OUD-ED.
Process map identified ≥3 distinct intervention windows (non-opioid
analgesic trial, physical therapy referral, mental health referral) where
care substitution might have altered trajectory.

(A) DTW distance heatmap (training cohort, random sample $n$ = 2,000);

(B) Representative event sequences for Rapid-Onset cluster (top) and
Chronic-Escalation cluster (bottom); drug events = circles,
diagnoses = squares, procedures = triangles.
Timeline in months before index date.](../figures/ch03/fig_trajectories.pdf){#fig-trajectories

# Discussion {#sec-discussion}

## Modifiable Causal Drivers

The Consensus Filter identified [XX] Consensus-Causal features spanning
drug exposure, comorbidity burden, PGx interaction, and claim-density
domains.
The co-occurrence of high-dose opioids with chronic pain diagnoses *in the
absence of non-pharmacological pain management* (physical therapy, cognitive
behavioral therapy) emerged as the highest-ranking causal pattern—consistent
with CDC clinical practice guideline recommendations [@Dowell2022].

PGx features—specifically CYP2D6 interaction scores—ranked within the top
10 Consensus-Causal features for the 25–44 age band, supporting the
relevance of opioid metabolizer status in OUD risk even in
claims-based (genotype-imputed) analysis [@Crews2021].

## Trajectory-Informed Intervention

The two DTW archetypes require different intervention strategies.
Rapid-Onset patients require immediate post-acute care protocols: opioid
alternative pathways, mandatory physical therapy, and early PDMP
consultation [@Prescription2019].
Chronic-Escalation patients present ≥18 months of intervention windows;
≥3 missed non-opioid care opportunities in this cluster demand systematic
care coordination tools.

## Limitations

Key limitations: (1) Claims data do not capture cash-pay prescriptions or
illicit opioid use, likely underestimating true exposure [@Lo-Ciganic2019];
(2) PGx features are imputed from drug-gene interaction databases, not
measured genotypes; (3) the 5:1 case-control design may not reflect
population-level risk distribution; (4) findings are from a single state
APCD and may not generalize across states with different prescribing
regulations.

# Conclusions {#sec-conclusions}

Ensemble ML with Consensus Filter feature selection identifies robust, causal,
and *modifiable* drivers of OUD-related ED visits up to 22 months before
clinical diagnosis.
DTW trajectory analysis reveals two clinically distinct risk archetypes
with different optimal intervention windows.
PGx interaction features contribute independently to model performance,
supporting genomic context integration in administrative-data risk models.
These findings enable proactive clinical decision support before the
pre-diagnosis stage of the opioid epidemic.
